findings: Homepage is one short paragraph and two images (a stock-style photo of mozzarella sticks and a banner of grinders and burgers); no hours, specials or menu highlights.
/menu.html is an empty page (header and footer only); the "Menu" link sends visitors to the eDiningExpress ordering page instead.
"Order Online" and "Delivery Available" are flat PNG images, not real buttons.
Old viewport tag with user-scalable=0 blocks pinch-zoom on phones.
Hours and contact are on separate thin pages; no social links, email or contact form anywhere.
Stored menu on eDiningExpress has 17 categories and 178 items with real photos, none of which appear on the shop's own site.
questions: Are the hours Tue-Sat 11 AM-8 PM, closed Sun and Mon, still right (the hours page says so)?
What are delivery zones, fees and minimums? The site only says "Delivery Available for Online Orders".
Is there a Facebook page or Instagram we should link? None is on the current site.
Is there a story to tell? The site only says "in business since 1973"; who founded it, and who runs it today?
Topping prices for build-your-own pizza and calzones were not on the public menu. Can you send them so we can show them on the site?

"Same Flavor, Every Way" links items by name (for example the Steak Bomb pizza, calzone and grinder; the Greek salad is paired with the Grecian). Are these the pairings you would make, and are any specialties missing?
Do you want to keep eDiningExpress for ordering? The new site links to it for every Order button.
The old homepage photos look like stock images. We used only the food photos from your eDiningExpress menu. Please confirm they are yours.
